### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via FieldPermissionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldPermissionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6a62c532ec67c9ee758095adc0e0f66b61676af1` — the merge of head `a4a95452fa24d62d0bc9157e87ec48d83e448c2e` into base `50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6a62c532ec67c9ee758095adc0e0f66b61676af1 && git checkout 6a62c532ec67c9ee758095adc0e0f66b61676af1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7 a4a95452fa24d62d0bc9157e87ec48d83e448c2e && git checkout -B drift-repro 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7 && git merge --no-ff a4a95452fa24d62d0bc9157e87ec48d83e448c2e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a4a95452fa24d62d0bc9157e87ec48d83e448c2e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts + content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts (`holdsSuperuserBypass`, `superuserFieldVote`, `fieldPermissionVote`, `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts (`resolveObjectPermission`, `superuserBypassSets`, `getFieldPermissions`, `conditionedFieldEntries`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts (`computeForbiddenFieldWrites`, `foldFieldRequiredPermissions`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-field-readers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts (the `fls` layer's `conditionedSentence`), docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md (the ⑧ note of 2026-11-02), content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx — the cited code is read, not reviewed. The remainder of the diff (`.changeset/29543-field-permission-superuser-vote.md`, the two regenerated `content/docs/references/**` pages) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #29543 (body and all four comments: triage 6585130976, claim 6586508051, claim amendment 6586583239, os-dev-report 6588036164), ruling 6573563853 on #29106 read in place, PR #29599 body, file list and net diff against `main` at the merge base e832ddb1, and the 65 check-runs on the head: every run that completed concluded `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 8/8, Test UI 16/16, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check Documentation Links, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate); the rest are `skipped` opt-in or matrix placeholders. No check is red or pending. The cited code is byte-identical between the merge base and the head (the merge commit brought no change to it).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The `hits` file changes two string literals only: the `when` key's `.describe(...)` text and the `FieldPermissionSchema` TSDoc docblock. No key, default, alias, guidance entry, refinement (`when` present ⇒ `readable !== false`) or `strictObject` surface moves. Nothing an author can write is added, refused or re-meant.
- **Public surface: the published `description` of `FieldPermission.when` changes — right, and declared.** The describe ships in `@objectstack/spec`'s `dist/` (JSON Schema + source `.zod.ts`) and is rendered into `content/docs/references/security/permission.mdx` (two `when` rows) and `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` (one `when` row). The three regenerated rows equal the new describe byte-for-byte; `Flag docs affected by code changes` and the `Lint · docs & code guards` family are green, so the generator produced them (Human Minimum 6/7 hold; the protocol.mdx row is generated output, no protocol source is touched, so the protocol freeze is honoured).
- **Behaviour: unchanged — right.** The vote the text now describes shipped in #29387 (`superuserFieldVote`, `holdsSuperuserBypass`, the post-merge application in `getFieldPermissions` and `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`). This PR only brings the published text to the code's side.
- **The TSDoc docblock hunk is inside the claim** — claim amendment 6586583239 added it (same file, same defect sentence). The runtime string (the describe) carries no tracker number; the ruling number sits in the TSDoc comment only, where the file already cites rulings. Right.
- The remaining stale wording on `main` (`git grep` of "only declaring" / "declaring sets vote" outside `content/docs/references`) is exactly the two edited sites; the sibling guide `field-level-security.mdx` already carried the super-user sentence from #29387 and agrees with the new callout.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/spec` — **right**. The diff publishes (a `dist/` description string changes), so `skip-changeset` would be wrong; `Metadata-protocol: none` (no key, accepted value, meaning or default of anything an author writes changes — the runtime meaning changed in #29387 in `core`/`plugin-security`, and this diff records it) ⇒ `patch`. The changeset body carries both declaration lines and no tracker number; it names the behaviour and "Nothing to migrate". `Check Changeset` is green.

`Clause-②:` line — `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and in the changeset, both line-initial, no arm. **Matches the diff**: no accept-set widening or narrowing. The card's Wanted asked for exactly `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch for spec.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1 (no assignee/reviewer set on the PR, MCP skipped): consistent with the dispatch's own ban on MCP and the hand-off rule; the seat sets them. Accepted.
- Deviation 2 (merge commit a4a95452 carries no trailers): it is a merge of `origin/main` with the default message, not an authored change; the edit commit de2dfacf is the authored one. Accepted.
- Deviation 3 (branch is the card-thread platform branch `claude/project-thread-pj50nk`, not `claude/issue-29543-…`): recorded in claim 6586508051 as a measured platform exception. Accepted; `Implemented-by:` below names that branch.
- Local gate `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED in the worktree: answered by the head's check-runs (`Build Core`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Packed-tarball smoke` is opt-in skipped). A describe string cannot change what a CJS entry loads. Closed.
- **Unfiled observation — `os explain`'s `conditionedSentence` overstates the lock for a Modify All holder: judged REAL, out of this PR's surface, should be filed.** `explain-engine.ts` (the `fls` layer) lists each row-conditioned entry from `conditionedFieldEntries` as "`field` (locked when …, set "…")" and says it is "judged per row by the write gate, applied as the lock everywhere else". For a caller whose sets hold `modifyAllRecords` on the object, `getFieldPermissions` applies `superuserFieldVote` AFTER the entry's vote under every verdict (`matched`, `unmatched`, `unjudged`), in the write gate (`computeForbiddenFieldWrites`), the row-blind readers and the record-scoped projection alike, so the entry is applied as a lock nowhere for that caller. The layer's hidden/partial mask is right (it reads the merged map); only the sentence is wrong, and in the restrictive direction (it reports a lock that does not bind). Report prose, not enforcement; no access is granted or withheld by it. Escalation: the seat files one follow-up card (domain:server, `os explain` fls layer, p3): either drop the per-row-lock sentence for a caller whose sets hold Modify All on the object, or append "overridden for the Modify All sets [names]". Not a FAIL for this PR — `explain-engine.ts` is outside the card's surface and the hits.
- The ruling's precondition (grep templates/examples for a set declaring both `viewAllRecords` and a `readable: false` entry) bound the runtime PR #29387, not this text PR. No flag.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged on the tree: every sentence the diff adds or rewrites in `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, read against `holdsSuperuserBypass`, `superuserFieldVote`, `getFieldPermissions`, `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`, `computeForbiddenFieldWrites` and `foldFieldRequiredPermissions` on the head; the `authorization.mdx` callout read against the same code because the describe and the callout are one statement in two renderings.

**The `when` describe (rewritten clause):**

1. "so the most-permissive merge across the caller's sets is unchanged: a set that locks a field only from a stage onward does not lock the rows before it, and a co-held set that says nothing about the field still lifts nothing, unless it holds the super-user bypass on the object (its own entry for the object, otherwise its `'*'` wildcard)." — **Holds.** `holdsSuperuserBypass` reads `objects[objectName] || objects['*']`: lookup, not merge, so an own entry without the bits withholds even under a wildcard that carries them, and the wildcard counts only when no own entry exists; the text says exactly that. Per object, not global: right. The private posture does not alter it (`resolveObjectPermission` withholds only a wildcard carrying neither bit), so leaving posture unsaid is neither wider nor narrower.
2. "Such a set votes on every field of the object, on every row, whatever `when` says: `viewAllRecords` votes `readable: true`, and `modifyAllRecords` votes `readable: true` and `editable: true`, so a row-conditioned lock never binds a Modify All holder." — **Holds.** `superuserFieldVote` returns `{readable: true, editable: true}` on `modify`, `{readable: true, editable: false}` on `view`, `null` otherwise; `getFieldPermissions` applies it after the per-entry `fieldPermissionVote`, whichever verdict the `judge` gave, and `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` applies it after its `unjudged` votes. The write gate calls `getFieldPermissions(objectName, sets, judge)` and then folds capabilities; the record-scoped projection's edit half is that gate; the row-blind readers call it without a judge. In every path a `matched` lock (`editable: false` on the named rows), an `unmatched` absence and an `unjudged` lock all end `editable: true` for a Modify All holder. "Every field": the code applies the vote to the fields the merge holds an entry for, and an undeclared field is already readable and writable (block-list posture, FLS guide), so the effective claim is the same — not wider. Tried: a set that declares `readable: false` on the field itself and holds View All — its own super vote lifts it, covered by "such a set votes on every field". Tried: a `when` entry whose row cannot be judged (predicate update, unreadable pre-image) — still `editable: true` after the vote; the sentence holds.
3. "View All never grants an edit." — **Holds.** `holdsSuperuserBypass(…, 'modify')` reads `modifyAllRecords` alone; the vote's `editable` is applied only when true, and the merge never lowers a bit.
4. "Otherwise union without deny is unchanged." — **Holds.** The per-entry merge is untouched; a caller holding no super-user set on the object is narrowed by a declared `readable: false` exactly as before (`superuserFieldVote` is `null`).
5. The sentences the diff keeps around the clause ("Readers that hold no row … report a row-conditioned entry as its lock, so a client never advertises an edit the gate refuses"; "The record-scoped field projection … judges the condition on the stored row exactly as the write gate does") remain true after the vote, because both readers apply the same `superuserFieldVote` as the gate.

**The `FieldPermissionSchema` TSDoc docblock:** "Beside the declaring sets, a set holding the super-user bypass on the object votes on every field of it, on every row …: `viewAllRecords` votes `readable: true`, `modifyAllRecords` votes `readable: true` and `editable: true`; View All never grants an edit. Otherwise union without deny is unchanged." — the same claims as 2–4; **holds**. It cites the ADR-0066 ⑧ note and ruling of record in a comment, as the file already does for the 2026-10-26 note.

**`content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`, FLS posture callout:**

6. "A set that holds View All (`viewAllRecords`) on an object also votes `readable: true` on every field of that object, and a set that holds Modify All (`modifyAllRecords`) votes `readable: true` and `editable: true`; View All never grants an edit." — **Holds** (2, 3). Per object: right.
7. "So no set's `readable: false` hides a field from a caller who holds a View All or Modify All set on its object" — **Holds**, and precisely scoped to a set's `readable: false` (the hide a merge can do). It does not claim a `maskingRule` or capability gate is lifted — see 8.
8. "a field's `requiredPermissions` capability gate still applies to every caller." — **Holds.** `foldFieldRequiredPermissions` runs AFTER `getFieldPermissions` in every enforcement reader on the head (write gate, result masker, query guard, object-wide and record-scoped projections, explain), and forces `{readable: false, editable: false}` whenever the caller's sets do not hold every listed capability — the super vote cannot reach it because it ran earlier. This is the ADR-0066 combination order (AND-gates first, grants union second), which the same page states above the callout. `isSystem` contexts skip FLS entirely, but they are not permission-set callers and the whole callout already speaks of callers in that sense.
9. "Otherwise union without deny is unchanged." — **Holds** (4).
10. "grant the object without those two bits to a set that must withhold a field from its own holders" — **Holds** and is the ADR note's own prescription. Because the own entry wins the lookup, an explicit object entry without the bits withholds even when the set's `'*'` wildcard carries them — the guidance is correct under both shapes.

**Width checks the brief asked for:** per object vs global — every sentence says "on the object" / "on its object"; the only global path is the `'*'` wildcard, which the describe names as the fallback. Read vs edit — View All read-only, Modify All read+edit, stated three times consistently. Row-conditioned `when` — the describe says the vote is row-blind and lands after `when`; code agrees in all three verdicts. Field-level overrides — a set's own `readable: false` on a field is overridden by its own or a co-held super vote; stated. `requiredPermissions` — stated as still binding; code agrees.

**Considered and not findings:** (a) an on-behalf-of request intersects the agent's merged map with the delegator's (ADR-0090 D10), so a lock in the delegator's sets binds the delegated write even when the agent holds Modify All — the describe, like every sentence in it and in the FLS guide, speaks of one caller's own merge, and D10 is documented as a global qualifier on its own page; (b) the `when` describe does not restate the `requiredPermissions` AND-gate — that gate is documented on `Field.requiredPermissions` and in the authorization page's fixed order, and the callout in this same PR names it.

**Findings in the `hits` file: none must-fix, none should-fix.** The text is neither wider nor narrower than the code on the head. The one real inaccuracy found lies in `os explain` report prose outside the card's surface (③, to be filed), not in the reviewed text.

- 风险与回滚：不改任何键、默认值或校验（+38 / -11）；回滚即 revert。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts` 的 `when` describe。

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:spec#5` · head `a4a95452fa24d62d0bc9157e87ec48d83e448c2e` · 2026-11-02T21:15Z

1. **Shape:** five files: `permission.zod.ts` (the `when` describe and the `FieldPermissionSchema` TSDoc), `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` (the FLS posture paragraph), the regenerated `references/security/permission.mdx` and `references/api/protocol.mdx` rows, and `.changeset/29543-field-permission-superuser-vote.md` (patch for `@objectstack/spec`). This matches claim 6586508051 as amended by 6586583239 (the TSDoc). No `protocol.zod.ts` source is touched; the `protocol.mdx` row is a generated artefact, so the freeze does not apply to it.
2. **Premise:** PR #29387 is merged, and the code it cites is byte-identical between the merge base and this head. Every added sentence holds against it: bypass is per object, with the object's own entry winning over `'*'`; View All makes a field readable and Modify All makes it readable and editable; a row-conditioned lock never binds a Modify All holder; `requiredPermissions` still applies to every caller.
3. **Gates:** 65 check-runs on this head: 57 success, 8 skipped (Lint UI because no `ui/` path is touched; the rest are opt-in harnesses), 0 failed. `mergeable_state` is clean.
4. **Contract review:** claim 6588486841. The isolated at-tier record 6588636490 is a **PASS** on this same head. Semver: patch is right (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`). The JSON-Schema description ships in dist, so `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.
5. **Not carried, recorded:** the dev's observation is confirmed. `os explain`'s FLS layer (`conditionedSentence` in explain-engine.ts) reports a row-conditioned lock as applying everywhere else. For a Modify All holder, `getFieldPermissions` overrides that lock, so the sentence overstates the restriction. It is report prose only and grants nothing. It is out of this card's surface, so the seat files a p3 domain:server follow-up.
6. **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 29599`: 0 of 5 paths, 49 changed lines ≤ 3000). The seat lands it via `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.
